questions.title: What guides the pollen tube?
questions.text: Identify the type of tropic movement that is responsible for the movement of the pollen tube towards an ovule.
steps: ① Tropism: directional growth towards or away from a stimulus
② Hydro = water, geo = gravity, photo = light
③ The ovule releases chemicals
④ The pollen tube grows towards these chemicals
∴ Chemotropism → (c)
questions.remember: Phototropism: light (shoot +). Geotropism: gravity (root +). Hydrotropism: water (root +). Chemotropism: chemicals (pollen tube).
questions.trap: Picking geotropism because the tube grows downwards. It's following chemicals from the ovule, not gravity.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 6 · Section 6.2.2 Movement due to growth
questions.tryit: Roots growing towards water show which tropism?

questions.title: Which way does a synapse signal go?
questions.text: In a synapse, the chemical signal is transmitted from:
opts: Dendritic end of one neuron to axonal end of another neuron.
Axon to cell body of the same neuron.
Cell body to axonal end of the same neuron.
Axonal end of one neuron to dendritic end of another neuron.
steps: ① Inside a neuron: dendrite → cell body → axon (electrical)
② At the axon's end, chemicals are released
③ They cross the gap (synapse) to the NEXT neuron
④ They start a new impulse in its dendrite
∴ Axonal end of one → dendrite of another → (d)
questions.ans: Option (d) Axonal end of one neuron to dendritic end of another neuron
questions.remember: Information flows one way: dendrite → cell body → axon → (synapse) → next dendrite. Electrical inside the neuron, chemical across the synapse.
questions.trap: Picking (b) or (c): those describe a path inside ONE neuron, but a synapse is a gap BETWEEN two neurons.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 6 · Section 6.1 (Fig. 6.1 structure of a neuron)
questions.tryit: Why does a nerve impulse travel in only one direction?
questions.tryans: Chemicals are released only at the axon end and received only at the dendrites

questions.title: The brain part for cycling
questions.text:
Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are activities which are possible due to coordination of which part of the brain?
(Part of the brain · Name of the area)
steps: ① Balance, posture, precise movement: cerebellum
② Cerebellum is part of the HIND-brain
③ Cerebrum (fore-brain): thinking, voluntary decisions ✗
④ Medulla (hind-brain): BP, salivation, vomiting ✗
∴ Hind-brain · Cerebellum → (c)
questions.remember: Fore-brain (cerebrum): thinking, senses, voluntary actions. Hind-brain: cerebellum (balance, posture, precision), medulla (BP, salivation, vomiting), pons (breathing).
questions.trap: Picking mid-brain cerebellum: the area is right but the cerebellum sits in the HIND-brain.
questions.tryit: Which part of the brain controls blood pressure and vomiting?

questions.title: True or false: the brain
questions.text:
Select the correct statements about the different parts of the brain.
(i) The thinking part of the brain is the forebrain.
(ii) Centres for smell, hearing, memory, sight are located in the forebrain.
(iii) Salivation, vomiting, blood pressure are controlled by the medulla in the hind brain.
(iv) Cerebellum does not control the posture and balance of the body.
steps: ① (i) Fore-brain is the thinking part ✓
② (ii) Smell, hearing, sight, memory centres: fore-brain ✓
③ (iii) Medulla controls salivation, vomiting, BP ✓
④ (iv) Cerebellum DOES control posture and balance ✗
∴ (i), (ii) and (iii) → (a)
questions.remember: Only statement (iv) is false: the cerebellum is exactly what controls posture and balance.
questions.trap: Rushing past the word 'NOT' in statement (iv). Read every statement for negative words.
questions.tryit: Name the part of the brain that controls breathing.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: iodine and goitre
questions.text:
Assertion (A): In case of iodine deficiency in our diet, there is a possibility that we might suffer from goitre.
Reason (R): One of the symptoms of goitre is swelling of neck.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① Thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxin
② Too little iodine ⟹ thyroid swells ⟹ goitre ✓ A true
③ A swollen neck is a symptom of goitre ✓ R true
④ But a symptom doesn't explain the CAUSE
∴ Both true, R not the explanation → (b)
questions.ans: Option (b) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.remember: Iodine is needed to make thyroxin. Deficiency ⟹ goitre (swollen neck). That's why salt is iodised.
questions.trap: Choosing (a) because both are true. Ask: does R say WHY A happens? A symptom doesn't explain the cause.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 6 · Section 6.3 Hormones in animals
questions.tryit: Why is iodised salt advised in our diet?
questions.tryans: Iodine is needed by the thyroid to make thyroxin; lack causes goitre

questions.title: Adrenaline: ready for danger
questions.text:
(a) Mention the gland and the hormone secreted by it in a scary situation in human beings.
(b) Write two responses that enable the human body to be ready to deal with such a situation.
steps: ① (a) Gland: adrenal gland (above the kidneys)
② Hormone: adrenaline, released straight into the blood
③ (b) Heart beats faster ⟹ more oxygen to the muscles
④ Blood to digestive system and skin is reduced, sent to muscles
⑤ Breathing rate rises (diaphragm and ribs contract faster)
∴ Adrenal gland · adrenaline · body ready for 'fight or flight'
questions.ans: (a) Adrenal gland; adrenaline · (b) heart beats faster, supplying more oxygen to muscles; blood to the digestive system and skin is reduced and diverted to skeletal muscles; breathing rate increases
questions.remember: Adrenaline is secreted directly into the blood by the adrenal glands and acts on the heart and other tissues to prepare the body for emergencies.
questions.trap: Naming the thyroid or pituitary. The emergency hormone is ADRENALINE from the ADRENAL gland.
questions.tryit: Where are the adrenal glands located?

questions.title: Feedback: how hormones are kept in check
questions.text: "The timing and the amount of hormone secreted by a gland are regulated in the human body." Justify this statement with the help of an example.
steps: ① Regulated by a feedback mechanism
② Example: blood sugar rises after a meal
③ Pancreas detects it and secretes more insulin
④ Insulin lowers blood sugar
⑤ As sugar falls, insulin secretion is reduced
∴ Feedback controls the timing and amount
questions.ans: Hormone secretion is regulated by feedback: e.g. when blood sugar rises, the pancreas releases more insulin; as sugar falls, insulin secretion is reduced
questions.remember: Feedback mechanisms keep hormone levels right: the result of a hormone's action switches its own secretion up or down.
questions.trap: Describing what insulin does without the 'reduces secretion when sugar falls' half: that half is the feedback.
questions.tryit: Which disease results from too little insulin?
